items.title: Trump Promotes Data Centers at Rally With Republican Facing Heat on Them
items.author: Tim Balk and Evan Gorelick
items.content: <article>The president defended the complexes, which have become a liability for Senator Jon Husted in a challenging midterm race.</article>

items.title: U.S.-Russia Talks on Ukraine Now Involve an Oil Deal Tied to Trump Allies
items.author: Anton Troianovski and Eric Lipton
items.content: <article>President Vladimir V. Putin brought up a sale of Russian energy assets with President Trump’s envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, pushing a deal that raises new questions about conflicts of interest.</article>

items.title: Trump Pitches Company Investment to Ohio Voters at Midterm Rally
items.author: Kate Sullivan
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump cited major corporate investment plans in Ohio during a rally in the state, part of his effort to boost Republican candidates in key races ahead of the midterm elections in November.</article>

items.title: Without Saying His Name, Ken Paxton’s Estranged Wife Tells Texans to Vote For Him
items.author: Lauren McGaughy
items.content: <article>In a new ad, the wife of Ken Paxton, who is divorcing him for alleged adultery, tells Texas voters to focus on the “whole team,” not “individual players.”</article>

items.title: 8 Key Findings From the Times/Siena Polls
items.author: Ruth Igielnik, Patricia Mazzei and Tim Balk
items.content: <article>Democrats are competitive in Alaska, Iowa, Ohio, Texas and even Kansas as they try to wrest control of the Senate from Republicans. Here’s a look at why.</article>

items.title: Australian Treasurer Calls US-Iran War an Economic ‘Disaster’
items.author: Matthew Brockett
items.content: <article>Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the US war with Iran has been an economic disaster, blaming the conflict for higher inflation and borrowing costs worldwide and warning it’s also damping global growth.</article>

items.title: Cornell President Says He Is ‘Deeply Disturbed’ by Rape Case
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said he was “deeply disturbed” by a student’s 2024 rape allegation that has drawn national outrage.</article>

items.title: North Korea’s Kim Oversaw Hypersonic Missile Drill, KCNA Says
items.author: Jaehyun Eom
items.content: <article>North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw the launch of an intermediate-range strategic missile using a hypersonic weapons system, state media said, underscoring his intent to further strengthen the country’s nuclear deterrent.</article>

items.title: In Alabama, Trump Relives His Glory Days (This Time With Some Empty Seats)
items.author: Shawn McCreesh
items.content: <article>The Deep South was the birthplace of the mega MAGA rally. How do people on the Gulf feel about President Trump now?</article>

items.title: Democrats May Have Found the Recipe for Flipping Red-State Senate Seats
items.author: Nate Cohn
items.content: <article>Five new Times/Siena polls continue a run of strong results for Democrats in states that President Trump won easily in 2024.</article>

items.title: With Elon Musk’s Return to Washington, Possible Conflicts of Interest Resurface
items.author: Kate Kelly
items.content: <article>The founder of SpaceX, with billions of dollars in military contracts, joins several other defense industry executives on a Pentagon advisory board.</article>

items.title: Trump Suggests Cornell Defendants Won’t Get a ‘Fair Shake’ From Letitia James
items.author: Katie Rogers
items.content: <article>President Trump weighed in on the case when asked about Ms. James, who has become a target of his second-term retribution campaign.</article>

items.title: How Trump’s Deportation Policies Have Rocked a South Florida House Race
items.author: Patricia Mazzei
items.content: <article>Representative María Elvira Salazar, a Republican, ran an ad criticizing the Trump administration. It may have jolted other Republicans — and drawn attention to her Democratic opponent.</article>

items.title: As Midterms Near, Justice Alito Says He Considers Each Year Whether to Retire
items.author: Abbie VanSickle
items.content: <article>The justice, the second oldest on the court at 76, told CBS News that he decided against stepping down last term. He could face pressure should Democrats win the Senate in November.</article>

items.title: Trump Urges Republicans to Vote By Mail After Criticizing Practice
items.author: Tim Balk and Evan Gorelick
items.content: <article>It was the latest mixed messaging from President Trump, who regularly votes by mail, but has made baseless claims that the practice is “inherently corrupt.”</article>

items.title: Latvian Leader Poised For Big Win in Election Shadowed by Putin
items.author: Aaron Eglitis
items.content: <article>Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’s party was on course to win the largest share of votes in an election on Saturday amid growing security threats from Russia, putting him in a strong position ahead of coalition talks to form the next government.</article>

items.title: Venezuela Sends FBI-Wanted Suspect to US in Sign of Deeper Ties
items.author: Andreina Itriago
items.content: <article>A Venezuelan national wanted by the FBI has been sent to the US to face trial, the latest sign of deepening law-enforcement cooperation between Caracas and the Trump administration.</article>

items.title: In Texas, Talarico’s Strength in Senate Polls Inspires a Democratic Dream
items.author: Robert Draper
items.content: <article>After a dry spell of more than three decades, Democrats are daring (yet again) to believe they can win one or more top-of-the-ballot races in a vast and stubbornly red state.</article>

items.title: Madrid Housing Protests Fuel Speculation Over Spanish Election
items.author: Clara Hernanz Lizarraga
items.content: <article>Thousands of people took to the streets of Madrid on Saturday, joining nationwide protests over housing costs that could increase pressure on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to call a snap election.</article>

items.title: G7 Fuel Release Offers Short Term Price Relief
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Economics economic statecraft lead Chris Kennedy tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the G7’s coordinated release of up to 100 million barrels of oil and fuel could provide near-term relief from record diesel prices, but will not resolve supply constraints tied to the Iran war and attacks on Russian refining capacity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kennedy says a US diesel export ban could create unintended consequences for domestic and global fuel markets, while high diesel costs are adding economic pressure in states with competitive midterm races  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Campaigns Deep in Republican Territory
items.content: <article>Bloomberg senior White House reporter Josh Wingrove tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s campaign stops in traditionally Republican states such as Alabama, Oklahoma and Texas reflect competitive races and an effort to bolster GOP support as economic concerns weigh on the party. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Wingrove also discusses Trump’s appearance with Dennis Rodman amid interest in renewed diplomacy with North Korea and an upcoming Alberta vote that could begin a process toward separation from Canada.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Greens Demand Thames Water Public Ownership, No Creditor Compensation
items.author: Lucy White
items.content: <article>UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is facing pressure to speed up his efforts to tackle the UK’s troubled water industry, as the Green Party called for Thames Water to be brought under public ownership immediately.</article>

items.title: Trump, Putin, Ukraine and an Oil Deal: 5 Takeaways
items.author: Eric Lipton and Anton Troianovski
items.content: <article>A proposal to bolster relations with the Kremlin through the purchase of Russian energy assets is striking even for an administration that regularly mixes personal business interests with foreign policy.</article>

items.title: Russia Strikes Major Kyiv Bridge as Drones Cross Into Moldova
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Russian forces hit a major bridge in Kyiv that connects the left and right banks of the Dnipro River, as well as a logistics center near the capital overnight, in the latest series of drone attacks on Ukraine’s civil infrastructure.</article>

items.title: Ukraine’s Surprise Counterattack Sets Back Putin’s Donbas Goals
items.author: Aliaksandr Kudrytski and Olesia Safronova
items.content: <article>Kyiv’s latest battlefield success has frustrated Vladimir Putin’s hopes of quickly seizing all of Ukraine’s Donetsk Region, a goal for the Russian president since he launched the full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.</article>

items.title: Pressure Builds on Iran as Trump Boosts US Military Presence
items.author: Peter Martin, Patrick Sykes, Fiona MacDonald and Samy Adghirni

items.title: Latvian Leader With Brash Style Poised for Re-Election

items.content: The party of recently-appointed Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs has dominated the race in a Baltic nation with the biggest Russian minority

items.title: Burnham’s Big Bet Has the UK’s Tories Sensing an Opportunity
items.author: Alex Wickham
items.content: <article>As the sugar rush of Andy Burnham’s barnstorming address to the Labour Party’s annual convention wears off, Britain’s unpopular Conservatives are beginning to think he might just have given them a shot at redemption.</article>

items.title: Trump Offering $90 Payments to 20 Million Medicare Recipients
items.author: John Harney
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump said his administration would soon send checks of “nearly $100” to more than 20 million older Americans to “help pay for their Medicare Part B premiums.”</article>

items.author: Madlin Mekelburg
items.content: <article>The US Justice Department urged a federal judge to reject a request by CNN, MS NOW and Politico for a longer court order that would prevent President Donald Trump from banning their journalists from the White House.</article>

items.author: Christina Jewett, Alice Callahan and Caroline Hopkins Legaspi
